interactiveMap.title: Interactive map
interactiveMap.desc: Drag systems, draw connections, set wormhole class / type / status per connection. Snap-to-grid and an optional minimap.

seedRegion.title: Seed a map from a region
seedRegion.desc: Spin up a new map pre-populated with an entire EVE region — every system laid out from CCP's 2D star-map projection (a Dotlan-style layout) with all stargate connections drawn. Pick a region when creating a map, or leave it blank for an empty one.

whIntel.title: Wormhole intel
whIntel.desc: Per-connection mass status (stable / destabilized / critical), end-of-life flag with countdown, K162-aware static identification, and frig-hole / gas-site auto-tagging from sig type.

rollingCalc.title: Rolling calculator
rollingCalc.desc: Plan and track collapsing a hole from its connection panel. Models the ±10% mass variance and forecasts each pass safe / may-collapse / will-collapse against the worst case. Define a roller ship (cold + prop-on mass, or pull your flown ship from ESI), step through passes with side-tracking that warns before a pass strands you on the far side, and see an "≈ N passes left" estimate. Cumulative mass syncs live to everyone viewing the hole.

whPicker.title: Wormhole type picker
whPicker.desc: Searchable popover for assigning the exact wormhole type to a connection. Statics quick-info on hover shows destination class, mass, and lifetime.

multiSelect.title: Multi-select bulk operations
multiSelect.desc: Shift-click to select multiple systems or signatures, then bulk-assign type, delete, or rename in a single action.

pngExport.title: PNG export
pngExport.desc: Render the current map — with sig counts, connections, and status — to a PNG you can drop into a fleet ping or a corp Discord.

sigAging.title: Wormhole sig aging
sigAging.desc: Wormhole sigs tint by their position in the WH type's known lifetime — yellow at 50%, orange at 90%, red past expected close. Catches forgotten chains before they collapse on someone.

brokenChain.title: Broken-chain detection
brokenChain.desc: Delete a wormhole sig and the connection it backed isn't left silently joined — it's quarantined: kept on the map but rendered severed (red dashed with a ✂ marker) and excluded from routing, so a collapsed chain is obvious instead of looking complete. Auto-restores if a sig backs the link again or you jump it.

orphanCleanup.title: Orphan cleanup
orphanCleanup.desc: One right-click sweep removes orphaned systems — those with no live connection, or only broken ones — while protecting your home and any locked systems. Keeps a working chain tidy without hunting down strays by hand.

lazyWhRemoval.title: Auto-remove aged wormholes
lazyWhRemoval.desc: Opt-in per map: a server-side sweep removes wormhole sigs once they pass their type's maximum lifetime, quarantining any connection they backed. Runs even when nobody has the map open, so synced and corp chains stay current on their own.

soloCorp.title: Solo / Corp split
soloCorp.desc: Every user has personal maps that are always private; in corp mode each corp also gets shared corp maps. Cross-corp visibility is opt-in via a single env flag.

multiCharacter.title: Multi-character accounts
multiCharacter.desc: Link your alts to one account and switch between them without logging in again — each character's maps merge in on link. Follow an alt's live location while you fly your main, and unlink a character whenever you like.

multiMap.title: Multi-map support
multiMap.desc: Each character (or corp) can maintain multiple independent maps up to configured limits — separate chains for separate ops without losing context.

mergeMaps.title: Merge maps
mergeMaps.desc: Fold one map into another. The destination is kept as the source of truth — only missing systems and connections are added, with signatures, structures, and notes merged in, and new systems slotted into the existing layout. Corp maps opt in per role as a merge source and/or destination.

crossMapSync.title: Cross-map sync
crossMapSync.desc: Have the same system on several maps? Opt in and scanning it on one map copies its signatures and anomalies to the same system on your others — personal maps sync with your other personal maps, corp maps with the corp's. Non-destructive: it only adds missing entries and fills blanks, never overwriting what you've already entered or deleting anything.

realtime.title: Real-time collaboration
realtime.desc: Edits sync live to everyone viewing the same map — systems, connections, rename/lock, signatures, structures, and merges all appear for other viewers within moments, no refresh. Streamed per map (you only get events for maps you can see), with your own changes echo-suppressed and an auto-resync on reconnect.

mapLocking.title: Map locking
mapLocking.desc: Admins can freeze a corp map's topology. Systems and connections lock for non-admins, but signatures, structures, and per-system notes stay editable so ops continue while the layout is pinned.

rbac.title: Role-based access
rbac.desc: Four tiers — readonly, edit, full, admin — gating corp-map actions. Personal maps stay yours regardless of role.

systemPanel.title: System panel
systemPanel.desc: Per-system cards for signatures, structures, NPC stations, notes, killboard, and activity charts. Cards are reorderable via drag-and-drop and persist per-user.

sigMgmt.title: Signature management
sigMgmt.desc: Paste straight from the probe scanner. Tracks created / updated age per signature, auto-deletes sigs missing from a re-paste, and supports bulk type assignment for multi-select.

structImport.title: Structure import
structImport.desc: Paste EVE overview data to import player-owned structures with names, types, owners, and notes in one operation.

autoStruct.title: Auto-discovered structures
autoStruct.desc: Your corp's citadels (via ESI when a member with the Station Manager role logs in) and any publicly-listed structures from a third-party feed appear automatically in the structures pane as read-only entries — already tinted by your standings toward the owner.

activityCharts.title: Activity charts
activityCharts.desc: 24-hour rolling history of jumps, ship / pod kills, and NPC kills per system, polled from ESI hourly. The poller persists data for every k-space system — not just ones someone has opened — so charts populate the moment you view a new system.

sovStation.title: Sovereignty & station data
sovStation.desc: Live alliance / corp / faction sov info and NPC station services, with in-game waypoint and destination actions.

killboard.title: Killboard pane
killboard.desc: Recent zKillboard activity per system, with NPC-only kills hidden by default (toggle to include). Rows tint red when a hostile actor is in the chain or a blue gets killed; blue when a friendly scores or a hostile dies. Recent kills also bubble up as highlights on the map.

effectDigest.title: Chain-wide effect digest
effectDigest.desc: A one-line summary at the top of the system info panel lists every Pulsar / Wolf-Rayet / Magnetar / etc. on the current chain. Hover for the modifier list; click to centre.

standings.title: Standings overlay
standings.desc: Your EVE contact list (personal, corp, and alliance — fetched via ESI on login and re-pullable on demand) drives a chain-wide visual layer. Sov holders show inline P/C/A standing pills; structures resolved via their EVE structure ID tint by owner-corp standing; sov-holder system nodes get a coloured halo so hostile territory stands out on the map.

scout.title: Scout connections
scout.desc: Thera and Turnur public Eve-Scout connections surfaced into the sidebar so you can jump straight to known holes.

a0.title: A0 sun detection
a0.desc: Auto-flags systems with A0 (yellow) suns visible via ESI for capital-friendly skirmish planning.

iceBelt.title: Ice belt systems
iceBelt.desc: Flags Empire-space systems that spawn ice anomalies with a ❄ icon — handy when staging mining ops or looking for an alternate harvest spot. Static dataset committed in-repo and resolved to system IDs at startup.

storms.title: Storm tracking
storms.desc: Active null-sec storms — Electric, Gamma, Exotic, Plasma — sourced from the community-maintained EveScout Rescue stormtrack feed surface as a colour-coded ⚡ on matching system nodes. Tooltip shows storm name, last report, and reporter. Refreshed every 30 minutes.

proximity.title: Proximity alerts
proximity.desc: Browser notification plus an audio ping when you're within a configurable number of jumps of an active incursion, pirate insurgency, or a sov-holding system whose corp / alliance you've set to red. Persistent toolbar chip shows the nearest threat at a glance.

watchlist.title: Watchlist
watchlist.desc: A personal, hand-edited list of holes you're hunting — a specific system, a wormhole type, or a characteristic (shattered, an effect, frig holes). Matches are highlighted on the map with your chosen marker and chime when they appear; one click jumps the view to any match.

discordNotif.title: Discord notifications
discordNotif.desc: Push corp chain intel to a Discord channel so alerts land even when nobody's watching the tab. Fires server-side on an inbound K162 or a new wormhole connection, scoped to corp maps. Admins filter which regions and maps notify from the admin panel. Best-effort and rate-limit-aware; bulk operations like region seeding never spam the channel.

routePlanner.title: Route planner
routePlanner.desc: Server-side BFS over stargates plus your live chain, so a route through a wormhole hop is a single click.

locationTracking.title: Location tracking
locationTracking.desc: Opt-in live character location dot in the toolbar, plus a per-map "you are here" indicator that updates every 10 seconds via ESI.

presence.title: Pilot presence
presence.desc: See where everyone viewing the same map is right now — a blue dot (pilot name on hover) marks each other viewer's current system, live as they jump. Covers anyone with the map open, not just your fleet; opt-in and nothing is stored.

onlineStatus.title: Online status
onlineStatus.desc: Toolbar dot shows whether each logged-in user is currently signed into EVE Online, so you can see at a glance who's actually on grid.

commandPalette.title: Command palette
commandPalette.desc: ⌘ / Ctrl + K opens a fuzzy search across systems, sigs, and actions — jump to a system, set a waypoint, or toggle a pane without touching the mouse.

homeHotkey.title: Home hotkey
homeHotkey.desc: Hit H to jump the viewport back to your home system from any panel. Right-click a system to set or change which one is home.

killHighlights.title: Recent-kill highlights
killHighlights.desc: Systems with kills in the last hour get a coloured halo so you can see fresh activity at a glance across the chain.

userStats.title: User stats modal
userStats.desc: Per-character totals: jumps, signatures by type, broken down by day / week / month / year / forever.

serverStatus.title: Server status widget
serverStatus.desc: Live Tranquility server status, player count, and ESI health in the toolbar. Cross-tab cached so all your open windows share a single ESI poll.

demoMap.title: Demo map
demoMap.desc: The landing page mounts a non-editable demo map so visitors can see what the tool does before logging in.

sidebar.title: Collapsible sidebar
sidebar.desc: Map Options, Connections, Proximity Alerts, Stale System Fade, and Shortcuts each expand or collapse independently. Per-section state persists per browser via localStorage.

colorVision.title: Colour-blind modes
colorVision.desc: Deuteranopia, protanopia and tritanopia palettes that re-map every status, class and standings colour across the app.

labels.title: System labels
labels.desc: Tag any system with coloured labels — toggle the built-in A/B/C and 1/2/3 set, or add up to three custom labels of your own (free text or a Phosphor icon) with a pick-your-own background colour. They render as pills above the node and sync to everyone on a corp map.

apiKeys.title: API key management
apiKeys.desc: Generate and revoke personal API keys to drive external tools against your maps. Each key acts as a chosen character and is scoped — read-only, read + live events, or read + write content — so it can only ever do what that character can.

chains.title: Saved wormhole chains
chains.desc: Record any path through your map as a named chain — pick a start and end system and the route is saved with its hop count. Hover a chain to dim everything off it and light up just its systems and connections, centre on any hop, and reorder your saved chains. Broken hops flag themselves for a re-scout.

jumpRange.title: Jump-drive range
jumpRange.desc: Pick a staging system and highlight every low/null system within jump range of it, colour-banded by ship class (Black Ops, Carrier, Super, JF) at your Jump Drive Calibration. Tag cyno-jump routes on connections, auto-annotated with the light-year distance and which classes can make the jump.

jumpPlanner.title: Jump planner
jumpPlanner.desc: Plot a multi-hop capital jump route between any two low/null systems. Pick a ship class and your skills, choose fewest jumps or least fuel, and see the route mapped with per-hop light-years and an isotope estimate. Save and reload your routes.

multiCorp.title: Multi-corp deployments
multiCorp.desc: CORP_ID accepts a comma-separated list of corporation IDs. One Nexum instance can host several corps; each corp's maps stay scoped to its own members unless CORP_MAP_SHARED=true.

allianceMaps.title: Alliance-wide maps
allianceMaps.desc: ALLIANCE_ID adds a third map scope above corp: alliance maps every member of the alliance can see. Set ALLIANCE_MAP_SHARED=true to share them across a coalition of alliances.

allianceRoles.title: Alliance admin role
allianceRoles.desc: A dedicated alliance_admin tier manages alliance maps and every member's role across the whole alliance — a superset of the corp admin. Any corp inside the alliance can still keep its own corp-private maps, no CORP_ID list needed.

adminDash.title: Admin dashboard
adminDash.desc: A dedicated /admin page with four tabs: Users, Maps, Reports, and Audit log. Admins reach it from the toolbar's Admin button.

userMgmt.title: User management
userMgmt.desc: Change roles, block / unblock, and force an ESI corp-membership re-check on demand. Self-block, self-demote, and changes to ADMIN_CHAR_ID are guarded against.

mapMgmt.title: Map management
mapMgmt.desc: Admins see every corp map with owner avatar, corp ticker, system / connection counts, lock state, and last-active time. Force-lock, force-unlock, and force-delete are one-click each.

usersReport.title: Users report
usersReport.desc: Per-character last login, systems added / deleted, structures added, signatures broken down by type, and last-corp-activity timestamps. Sortable, filterable by activity and time window, exportable as CSV.

systemsReport.title: Systems report
systemsReport.desc: Aggregate corp-map signatures with a sig-type donut, a daily / monthly activity line chart (bucketing adapts to the window), and a sortable wormhole-type breakdown.

timeWindowed.title: Time-windowed reporting
timeWindowed.desc: Every report can be scoped to past 24 hours, week, month, year, or all time. Chart bucketing adapts automatically: hourly for 24h, daily for week / month, monthly for year and all-time.

auditLog.title: Audit log
auditLog.desc: Every admin action — role change, block / unblock, force-lock, force-delete, ESI corp change, auto-block on corp departure — is recorded with actor, target, old → new value, and timestamp. Exportable as CSV.

corpTicker.title: Corp ticker resolution
corpTicker.desc: Corp IDs in the Users and Maps reports are resolved to in-game tickers via ESI, with a 1-hour in-memory cache to keep report loads cheap.

perCharAttr.title: Per-character attribution
perCharAttr.desc: Sigs, structures, and system add / delete actions are recorded with the user who made them, so reports can answer "who has been scanning what" with no manual logging.

accessControl.title: User access control
accessControl.desc: Decide who can sign in beyond your .env core: a DB allow-list (seeded from CORP_ID/ALLIANCE_ID) managed in the admin area, optional auto-admit of friendly corps/alliances by in-game standing (+5/+10), and a standings viewer that groups your contacts by band. Sessions are re-checked live, so revoking access — or a pilot leaving an admitted corp — logs them out.

landing.forCorpsBody: Run Nexum as a shared deployment for your corp or alliance. Members get visible-to-the-corp chain maps and private personal maps in one tool, with role-based permissions, admin tooling, and per-character activity reporting.
landing.compareBody: See how Nexum stacks up against Pathfinder, Tripwire and Wanderer — features, hosting and cost, side by side.
landing.languagesBody: Nexum is fully translated into nine languages — and it auto-detects yours from your browser the first time you visit. Prefer a different one? Switch any time from the language picker in the toolbar.
landing.compareLink: Compare Nexum vs Pathfinder, Tripwire & Wanderer →
landing.helpLink: New here? Read the how-to guide →
landing.discordCtaBody: Drop into the Nexum Discord — feedback, feature requests, scanning chat and o7s all welcome.
landing.aboutBody1: Nexum is a wormhole and exploration tool. It can be used for mapping routes and logging signatures. It was heavily inspired by Pathfinder — but with Pathfinder no longer actively developed (no new release since 2020), rather than complain about it, Nexum was created.
landing.aboutBody2: Nexum is built by a single developer. I'm adding features as we go but get in contact if you want support or feature requests
landing.aboutMe:
Nexum is written by Addelee as a solo project. I've played eve since Beta back in 2003. You might see me hanging out in the Help channels or the Scanning channel. I've played in all areas of space from living in wormholes and thera, running missions in High Sec, gate camping in lowsec and now, null life with Goonswarm.



As a day job, I am a programmer and run Area 404. Because of this, I decided I'd write this tool. I'm an avid explorer in Eve therefore I wanted a tool that worked for me.



Nexum is open source and I welcome anyone to contribute. I would definitely appreciate feedback and any bugs you encounter so please flag things on GitHub
landing.techStack1: Nexum is held together with the finest space-age materials money and caffeine can buy. The frontend is React with TypeScript — because arguing with a compiler is still more productive than arguing with a nullsec alliance. Maps are rendered with ReactFlow, which handles all the node-dragging shenanigans so I didn't have to. State is managed by Zustand, which is delightfully small and has never once told me to "just use Redux".
landing.techStack2: The backend is Node.js with Express — proven, boring, and it works. Data lives in PostgreSQL, seeded with CCP's Static Data Export so Nexum actually knows what J213422 is without asking the ESI every five seconds. Authentication is handled by EVE Online SSO — your credentials never touch this server, which is exactly how it should be.
landing.techStack3: Live system intelligence comes from the EVE ESI (CCP's official API) and kill data from zKillboard. The whole thing is containerised with Docker and proxied through nginx, because someone has to keep the lights on while you're getting evicted from your wormhole.

whyNexum.a: Nexum is the Latin word for a bond or connection — which felt appropriate for a tool built around mapping the connections between wormhole systems. It also sounds vaguely like something you'd find floating in a C6 magnetar, which was really the deciding factor.

multipleAccounts.a: Yes — each EVE character gets their own set of maps. Just log in with a different character via EVE SSO and Nexum will keep their maps completely separate. No cross-contamination, no accidental sharing of your super-secret wormhole chain with your alt corp.

dataSafe.a: Nexum never sees your EVE password — authentication is handled entirely by CCP's EVE SSO. The only thing stored is your character identity and the maps you build. Your map data lives in a private database and is not shared with anyone. That said, don't use Nexum for your alliance's top-secret invasion route — no tool on the internet is a substitute for good operational security.

reportBugs.q: Can I report bugs, add feedback and request features?
reportBugs.a: Absolutely. The project is open source on <gh>GitHub</gh> — open an issue for bugs or feature requests, or submit a pull request if you're feeling brave. Feedback via in-game mail to the character tied to this account also works if GitHub isn't your thing.

runYourself.a:
Yes — Nexum is fully self-hostable. The source is on GitHub and the whole stack spins up with a single docker compose up. You'll need to register your own EVE application on the CCP developer portal to get SSO credentials, but beyond that the README covers everything — including importing the EVE static data and pointing Traefik at it if that's your thing. If something breaks, open an issue. If you fix it, please open a PR.



It isn't the most technical thing to run up but I'd recommend you have basic knownledge of docker and whatever server your running on (Linux?)

goonTrust.q: But you're a Goon, why would we trust you?
goonTrust.a: Fair question, and honestly the correct instinct to have in New Eden. The code is fully open source — you're welcome to read every line, run it yourself, or have someone you trust audit it. Nexum has no interest in your scouting routes, your corp's killboard shame, or whatever you've got parked in that C5. The worst thing a Goon has ever done in a wormhole is get evicted from one, and I'd like to help you avoid that fate.

roadmap.q: Do you have a roadmap for new features?
roadmap.a:
Loosely. Currently the system only works with solo players. The next logical thing would be to implement this for Corporations and Alliances. Once I iron out any bugs from this initial launch, I'll start work on that.

This does assume real life work doesn't get in the way!



If you have any pressing feature you want, drop me a message ingame and we can chat.

donateIsk.a: I prefer it if you did not, no. I'm not doing this for ISK so keep it and spend it on something to blow up in or blow someone else up in!

announcer.delayNote: Voice may be delayed by up to 5 seconds. The first run takes longer.

mapSidebar.bookmarkHelp: On a wormhole signature row, click the copy icon to copy a paste-ready bookmark name, then paste it into the in-game bookmark. Build the name with these tokens:
mapSidebar.canvasNotFound: Could not find the map canvas
mapSidebar.collapseGraceHint: How long an expired wormhole waits before it's severed and its signatures removed.
mapSidebar.copyFailed: Copy failed — select and copy manually
mapSidebar.corpSkipKspaceHint: When on, no one on this map records K-space jumps. Only owner/admins can change this.
mapSidebar.crossMapSync: Sync system data across my maps
mapSidebar.crossMapSyncHelp: When you add or edit signatures and anomalies on a system, copy them to the same system on your other maps (personal maps sync with your other personal maps; corp maps with the corp's other maps). Non-destructive: it only fills in missing or blank entries — it never overwrites data you've already entered or deletes anything.
mapSidebar.fleetHint: Render fleet-mates as purple dots on the system they're in. Hover a dot to see the names.
mapSidebar.densityHint: Spacing around panel text. Font size is separate, so you can keep large text in tighter chrome.
mapSidebar.hidePresenceHint: Other people viewing this map won't see where you are. Your own you-are-here marker is unaffected, and this is separate from tracking jumps.
mapSidebar.importWandererTitle: Import a map exported from the Wanderer mapper (creates a new personal map)

jumpRange.pickHint: Search a staging system above, or right-click a system on the map and choose “Jump range from here”.
jumpRange.noCoords: This deployment doesn't have 3D system coordinates loaded, which jump range needs. Run the coordinate backfill on the server (or re-run setup-db), then reload.

mapSidebar.lazyRemoveWhHint: Periodically removes wormhole signatures older than their type's maximum lifetime. If the sig backed a connection with nothing else holding it, the connection is marked broken (quarantined) rather than deleted. Runs server-side, so it applies even when the map isn't open.
mapSidebar.mapBookmarkHelp: When set, everyone on this map copies bookmarks in this format. Leave blank to let each user use their own format.
mapSidebar.mergeFlagHint: When on, corp members can use this corp map as the source or destination of a merge.
mapSidebar.mergeHint: Combine another map into one of yours. The destination keeps its existing systems; missing systems, links, and the data you select are added or updated. This can't be undone.
mapSidebar.notNexumMap: File does not look like a Eve-Nexum map export.
mapSidebar.notWandererMap: File does not look like a Wanderer export.
mapSidebar.importPathfinderTitle: Import a map exported from Pathfinder — its Map settings, Export tab (creates a new personal map)
mapSidebar.pathfinderImported: Imported from Pathfinder: {{systems}} systems, {{connections}} connections ({{skipped}} skipped).
mapSidebar.notPathfinderMap: File does not look like a Pathfinder export.
mapSidebar.notifBlockedHint: Browser is blocking notifications for this site. Click the lock icon in your address bar → Notifications → Allow → reload the page.
mapSidebar.notifBlockedTooltip: Click the lock / site-info icon in your address bar → Notifications → Allow, then reload.
mapSidebar.notifHint: Choose which events alert you, and how. Desktop notifications need the browser permission above.
mapSidebar.notifExitsHint: Alerts once when an exit of at least this security appears on the chain. Off by default.
mapSidebar.panelLayoutTooltip: Where the system panel sits: beneath the map, or beside it as a tall column on the right.
mapSidebar.proximityHint: Ping when an incursion, insurgency, or hostile-sov system is within range of your current location.
mapSidebar.proximityNotifyHint: Toggle the desktop notification and sound for this in the Notifications section below.
mapSidebar.reclassifyGatesTooltip: Retype wormhole links that are actually stargates (gate-adjacent systems) as gates
mapSidebar.routeHint: Shortest: fewest jumps regardless of security. Secure: prefer high-sec, detour through low/null only when no high-sec path is available.
mapSidebar.routeShortcutNote: Routes using a wormhole, Thera, Turnur, or jump gate can't be set as an in-game destination or waypoint — right-click a k-space system in the route to set one to it instead.
mapSidebar.shareActiveHint: Live share link. Toggle below to change what guests see. If a link was previously generated, the changes will take effect automatically and you DO NOT need to regenerate.
mapSidebar.shareInactiveHint: Create a read-only link anyone can open without an account. Pick categories to expose and an expiry window — anyone holding the URL within that window can see everything you opted in.

shortcut.overwriteSigs: Paste signatures in overwrite mode (remove despawned)
shortcut.vivaldiNote: Vivaldi (and some other browsers) bind Ctrl+Shift+V to their own command, so it never reaches Nexum. Turn on 'Overwrite on paste' and use plain Ctrl+V instead, or rebind the shortcut in your browser's keyboard settings.

mapSidebar.siteBookmarkHelp: On a relic, data, or gas signature row, click the copy icon for a paste-ready bookmark name. Build it with these tokens:
mapSidebar.skipKspaceHint: When on, only records the K-space system you first jump into from J-space and the last one before you jump back into J-space — skipping everything you gate through in between. HS/LS/NS only; Pochven is always tracked.
mapSidebar.spreadNodesTooltip: Adjust system nodes to stop overlapping
mapSidebar.staleHint: Visually dim systems that haven't been updated for the chosen interval, so old chain residue is easy to spot at a glance.
mapSidebar.tidyLayoutTooltip: Snap known systems back to their real in-game map positions
mapSidebar.untangleLayoutTooltip: Rearrange by connections (not geography) to pull linked systems together and shorten crossing lines
mapSidebar.wandererImported: Imported from Wanderer: {{systems}} systems, {{connections}} connections ({{skipped}} skipped).
mapSidebar.panelColumnsTooltip: Splits the panel's panes into side-by-side columns, so notes or the killboard can sit beside signatures instead of below them.

proximityOptIn.title: Enable threat alerts?
proximityOptIn.body: New Eden is a dangerous place. Nexum can give you a desktop notification and a short audio ping when you're within a few jumps of an active incursion or insurgency — so you don't blindly autopilot into one.
proximityOptIn.sub: You can change the threshold or turn this off at any time in Map Options → Proximity Alerts.

tripwire.title: Importeren uit Tripwire (experimenteel)
tripwire.buttonTitle: Haal een Tripwire-keten binnen, met de signaturen
tripwire.step1: Open je Tripwire-tabblad en log in zoals gewoonlijk.
tripwire.step2: Open de browserconsole (F12), plak het script hieronder en druk op Enter. Het verzamelt je Tripwire-kaart en kopieert die naar het klembord - bij een lange keten duurt dat een paar seconden. Voer het één keer uit, vanuit elk systeem.
tripwire.step3: Plak het hier en importeer. Er wordt nooit om je Tripwire-wachtwoord gevraagd.
tripwire.extraHint: Alleen nodig voor systemen die niet in je keten zitten. Tripwire kan die niet opsommen, dus noem ze hier en dan worden ze ook nagekeken.
tripwire.scopeNote: Dit haalt je keten binnen met de signaturen van elk systeem, de wormgattypes, de massa en resterende levensduur van elk gat, en de notities die erop staan. Waar jouw Tripwire het toestaat komt het hele masker mee, inclusief systemen die nooit iemand verbonden heeft; waar dat niet kan, meldt de console dat. Het komt binnen als een nieuwe persoonlijke kaart.
